# Car Calculator (carcalculator.com.au)

> A free Australian calculator, presented by Crown Money, that compares the true
> cost of owning the same car three ways — buying outright with cash, a secured
> car loan, or a salary-packaged novated lease — using FY 2026-27 income tax,
> FBT, GST, the EV exemption and state-by-state stamp duty. Every assumption is
> editable and every figure is sourced.

## Calculators on the page (tabs; deep-linkable by URL hash)

1. Buy vs loan vs lease comparison (#calculator) — the flagship tool
2. Car loan repayments (#loan) — repayment, interest, balance by year
3. Novated lease estimate (#novated) — package, tax saved, ECM, residual
4. Stamp duty & rego (#duty) — your state plus all 8 side by side
5. Fuel & charging cost (#fuel)
6. Depreciation (#depreciation) — average curve or custom %, 1-10 years
7. Fuel economy (#economy) — L/100km, km/L, MPG conversions
8. CO2 emissions (#emissions) — petrol/diesel/hybrid/EV incl. grid factor
9. EV vs petrol break-even (#breakeven)

## What it answers

- "Is a novated lease cheaper than a car loan or paying cash in Australia?"
- "How much cheaper is an EV on a novated lease?" (FBT exemption for battery
  EVs under the $91,661 LCT fuel-efficient threshold, FY 2026-27)
- "What will this car really cost me over 1-5 years?" — including what the
  money would have earned invested (mortgage offset, savings, or shares,
  after tax), not just cash out the door.

## Methodology (summary)

- Same car, same term, same end point for all three methods; the user chooses
  whether to credit a sale of the car at the end or keep it (in which case its
  remaining value is shown but not subtracted).
- Income tax: FY 2026-27 resident brackets (0/15/30/37/45%), 2% Medicare levy,
  LITO. Tax savings computed as the exact tax difference at the user's salary.
- Novated lease: financier claims GST on the car (capped at $6,353), running
  costs packaged ex-GST, FBT neutralised by the Employee Contribution Method
  (20% of base value post-tax, plus the 1/11 GST the employer remits on that
  contribution), ATO minimum residuals (28.13% at 5 years) plus 10% GST on
  the residual payout. Battery EVs under the threshold are fully FBT-exempt
  and 100% pre-tax.
- Stamp duty: current schedules for NSW, VIC, QLD, SA, WA, TAS, NT and the
  ACT, including EV concessions in force at July 2026.
- Opportunity cost: every outflow in every method is future-valued at the
  user's after-tax investment return, so cash, loan and lease are treated
  identically.
- Market defaults (July 2026): secured car loan ~7.5% p.a. comparison rate,
  novated lease ~9.5% p.a. effective, comprehensive insurance ~$1,400/yr,
  petrol ~$1.80/L, per-state rego+CTP. All editable.

## Key facts (FY 2026-27, sources: ato.gov.au and state revenue offices)

- Income tax brackets: $0-18,200: 0% · $18,201-45,000: 15% · $45,001-135,000:
  30% · $135,001-190,000: 37% · $190,001+: 45% (+2% Medicare levy)
- FBT rate 47%; statutory formula 20%; FBT year ends 31 March 2027
- EV FBT exemption threshold: $91,661 (LCT fuel-efficient, at first retail
  sale); PHEVs not exempt since 1 April 2025
- Car limit $69,883 → max GST credit on a car $6,353
- ATO minimum lease residuals: 65.63% (1yr), 56.25% (2yr), 46.88% (3yr),
  37.50% (4yr), 28.13% (5yr) — ATO ID 2002/1004

## Important caveats

General information only, not financial, tax or credit advice. Does not model
HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, super, or business-use
deductions. Novated lease quotes vary widely between providers.

## About

Presented by Crown Money (https://www.crown.money/). Figures reviewed July 2026;
year-dependent constants live in one data file and are updated annually.
